sections.h2: Where is the Auglaize County Recorder and when is it open?
sections.html:
The recorder's office is at 209 S. Blackhoof St., Suite 103, in Wapakoneta, Ohio 45895. The office keeps weekday hours, opening at eight in the morning and closing at half past four, and the phone is 419-739-6735. The fax line is 419-739-6736.

The county treasurer works from the same building, at 209 S. Blackhoof Street, with a separate line at 419-739-6745. A seller closing a deed can often handle both the recording and the tax payoff in one trip.

sections.h2: What does the Auglaize County Recorder keep on file?
sections.html:
The recorder maintains a complete, permanent record of every document that conveys or encumbers land in the county. Property records begin in 1848, the year the county was formed. The office files each document, indexes it, keeps the books in archival form, and makes them available to the public.

  • It enforces more than 1,000 sections of the Ohio Revised Code that touch the recorder's duties.
  • It sits on the county records commission, which approves how long county records are kept.
  • It runs the county microfilming department.
  • It collects filing fees and pays them into the county general fund.
  • It notifies the commissioners and township trustees each year of their duty to file zoning resolutions, maps and amendments.

The county posts a fee schedule on the recorder's page, marked as updated October 24, 2024. Use that schedule for the amount to send with a deed.

sections.h2: What recording fees does Ohio law set?
sections.html:
ORC 317.32 lists the statewide fee structure, and the county's schedule operates within it. The page below uses the statute's own wording because it applies in Auglaize County as in every other Ohio county.

Recording fees under ORC 317.32 that apply in Auglaize County
ServiceBase feeHousing trust fund fee
Recording and indexing, first two pages$17$17
Each subsequent page$4$4
Marginal reference by separate instrument$2$2
Certified copy, per page$1$1
Local fax or electronic transmission, per page$1$1

On top of those, a county may charge a document preservation surcharge of up to five dollars, which goes to the county general fund. Ask the Auglaize County Recorder what the posted schedule shows.

sections.h2: Who collects the deed transfer fee in Auglaize County?
sections.html:
The auditor does, and the auditor's office is a separate stop from the recorder. The auditor maintains records of deed transfers, homestead exemptions, oil and gas wells, special assessments and all real property, including exempt parcels. Before it endorses a deed, the buyer files a statement of value under ORC 319.202.

The fee under ORC 319.54(G)(3) is one dollar, or ten cents for each one hundred dollars or fraction of value, whichever is greater. The grantor pays it. A county may also levy a transfer tax under Chapter 322, so ask the auditor whether Auglaize County does. Some transfers are exempt, including a transfer made only to give or release security for a debt, a transfer under a court order that is not itself a sale, and a transfer to correct a deed already recorded.

sections.h2: How are Auglaize County values set and challenged?
sections.html:
The auditor is the county's chief assessor. By the county's description, the auditor must reappraise all real property every six years and update values every three years. A complaint about value goes to the Board of Revision, which the county describes as the auditor, the treasurer and one county commissioner, who hear testimony and research the complaint.

Under ORC 5715.19(A)(1) the complaint is due by March 31 of the following tax year or the close of first-half collection, whichever is later. A postmark on a mailed complaint counts as the filing date, as long as it is a United States Postal Service postmark and not a private meter. The treasurer's page links to a delinquent land tax notice for tax year 2025, so ask that office whether a parcel you plan to sell appears on it.

sections.h2: What is Auglaize County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Auglaize County in northwestern Ohio was founded on February 14, 1848 and is named for the Auglaize River. It covers 402 square miles, which makes it the second-smallest Ohio county by area. The county is crossed by the Auglaize River and the Miami and Erie Canal, and it holds the headwaters of the St. Marys, Great Miami and Scioto rivers plus parts of Grand Lake and Lake Loramie. Wapakoneta holds the courthouse and is the biggest city, and Saint Marys is the second.

  • The 2020 census found 19,873 housing units, of which 6.4% were vacant, and 75.6% of occupied homes were owner-occupied.
  • The median age was 41.3, and 19.4% of residents were 65 or older.
  • Manufacturing anchors the economy, and employers with more than 400 workers include Crown Equipment, Minster Machine, Veyance Technologies, Dannon and Joint Township District Memorial Hospital.

With so many owner-occupied homes, most sales here are ordinary house-to-house deeds. Heirs selling a parent's house or an owner moving out of state can close as-is, and the recording steps stay the same.

sections.h2: What do the Auglaize County treasurer and auditor handle for a seller?
sections.html:
The treasurer collects local taxes, particularly real property and personal taxes, and also taxes on manufactured homes, hotel-motel stays and special assessments. The office keeps the money collected for schools, cities, townships and villages safe until it is distributed. Its staff is small, two full-time employees, so call ahead for a payoff figure rather than showing up on closing day.

The auditor does the assessing. Beyond reappraisals, the auditor registers manufactured homes and assesses their value, then passes the proceeds to municipalities, townships and school districts in proportion. The auditor also sits on the county budget commission with the treasurer and the prosecuting attorney, which oversees the tax rates set by other political subdivisions.

  • Payoff and delinquent balances: treasurer, 419-739-6745.
  • Statement of value, homestead and parcel records: auditor.
  • Deed and mortgage recording: recorder, 419-739-6735.

sections.h2: What should I bring to record a deed?
sections.html:
Bring the signed and acknowledged deed, the statement of value that the auditor has endorsed, and payment for the fee shown on the county schedule. If you are mailing the deed, call 419-739-6735 first to confirm the total. Keep a copy of the last recorded deed, since the legal description must match.

If the deed will go to a title company, the company usually records it for you after closing, and the recorder's index then shows the new owner.

faqs.q: What are the Auglaize County Recorder's hours?
faqs.a: Weekdays from eight in the morning until half past four. The office is at 209 S. Blackhoof St., Suite 103, Wapakoneta, and the phone is 419-739-6735.

faqs.q: How far back do Auglaize County property records go?
faqs.a: To 1848, according to the recorder's page. The office keeps permanent land records in archival form and makes them available to the public.

faqs.q: How much does the recorder charge for a deed?
faqs.a: The statute sets $17 plus a $17 housing trust fund fee for the first two pages and $4 plus $4 for each later page. The county's posted schedule, updated October 24, 2024, shows its current totals.

faqs.q: Who collects the transfer fee when a house sells?
faqs.a: The county auditor, at one dollar or ten cents per hundred dollars or fraction of value, whichever is greater. The grantor pays it, plus any county transfer tax under Chapter 322.

faqs.q: Where do I challenge my property value?
faqs.a: File a complaint with the county auditor for the Board of Revision by March 31 of the following tax year or the close of first-half collection, whichever is later. The auditor must reappraise every six years.
